The peer-reviewed J. Stat. Comput. Simul. paper comparing against other ziggurats could not be opened (tandfonline/arXiv blocked), so not B.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 13 stars, 5 forks; algorithm ported to Apache Commons RNG (ZigguratSampler, whose JMH ZigguratSamplerPerformance benchmark compares it with the older Marsaglia-Tsang ZigguratNormalizedGaussianSampler), chosen per WebSearch snippets as the default for JDK 17 RandomGenerator nextGaussian/nextExponential, USGS BiF Fortran port, PyPI fast_prng
corrections.caveats: The listed baselines (std::mt19937, PCG, xoshiro) are uniform generators, not normal samplers; the real comparison is against other ziggurat implementations (Doornik, Marsaglia-Tsang). No head-to-head against std::normal_distribution or Boost found. Paper abstract (J. Stat. Comput. Simul. 86(7), 2016; arXiv 1403.6870) says median runtimes for exponential and normal variates are reduced to 58% and 53% (range 41-93%); seen only in a WebSearch snippet (snippet only). README states Alex Herbert later fixed two bugs (fast rejection in the normal sampler, off-by-one overhang derivative indexing), so the paper's timings were measured on code later fixed for correctness bugs. Commons RNG reports its Java port beats its older ziggurat on JDK 8 and is no worse on later JDKs (WebSearch snippet; Java port, not this C code). The last commit (2025-05-21) only added a LICENSE file. timings.csv referenced by benchmarks/profile_all.py returns 404 at HEAD.

notes: README number confirmed verbatim; no baseline numbers in repo. Last commit 2025-05-21 is about 16 months old, so stale (record already said stale). Notable beyond its 13 stars through the Commons RNG and JDK 17 adoption.

tier_reason: First-party OBR benchmark CSVs in hpsim/OGL_DATA (boxTurb16, OGL v0.1-108) time OpenFOAM native CG/BiCGStab ('OF', reference) on an Intel Xeon Gold 6230 against Ginkgo CG/BiCGStab on a Tesla V100 and OpenMP, with hardware named but no compiler or flags, so C. The peer-reviewed Meccanica 2024 paper (which could support B) is blocked here (springer, d-nb.info) and was seen only as WebSearch snippets.

corrections.claimed_speedup: OGL_DATA boxTurb16 (OGL v0.1-108, June 2021) pressure solve, median run_time (derived from page data): resolution 64, unpreconditioned CG: OpenFOAM native on 1 Xeon Gold 6230 process 36.04 s vs Ginkgo CUDA on Tesla V100 21.93 s (about 1.64x); BiCGStab 46.92 s vs 23.42 s (about 2.0x). At resolution 32 the GPU is slower (CG 2.20 s OpenFOAM vs 3.14 s V100), and Ginkgo OpenMP at res 64 (best 37.6 s) does not beat single-process OpenFOAM CG. Meccanica 2024 paper (snippet only): up to 8x over non-accelerated execution for lidDrivenCavity3D with 76 and 32 MPI ranks, and about 15x largest GPU-versus-CPU speedup on one machine.
corrections.hardware: OGL_DATA boxTurb16 run: Intel Xeon Gold 6230 @ 2.10GHz (OpenFOAM native and Ginkgo OMP) and NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB (Ginkgo CUDA)
corrections.baseline: OpenFOAM native CPU linear solvers (PCG/PBiCGStab, unpreconditioned in the OGL_DATA runs); not SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc
corrections.caveats: OGL contains no solver kernels of its own; it is a Ginkgo wrapper (README: 'OGL is a wrapper for ginkgo solvers and preconditioners'). Its only extra evidence is OpenFOAM-integration timings: OGL_DATA CSVs (first-party, no compiler or flags; GPU vs single CPU process, hardware-confounded; GPU loses at small sizes) and the Meccanica 2024 paper (Olenik, Koch, Boutanios, Anzt, doi 10.1007/s11012-024-01806-1) whose numbers were seen only in WebSearch snippets (about 15x on one machine; up to 8x for lidDrivenCavity3D vs 76/32 MPI ranks). License: README SPDX header GPL-3.0-or-later, LICENSES/ also holds MIT and Unlicense texts (REUSE layout), so some files carry different terms.

notes: Fold candidate: OGL wraps Ginkgo (already listed at B). It does carry OpenFOAM-specific measurements Ginkgo's entry lacks (Ginkgo vs OpenFOAM's native PCG/PBiCGStab inside OpenFOAM runs, about 1.6-2x on a V100 at the largest boxTurb16 size per OGL_DATA, up to 8-15x per the Meccanica snippets), but no new kernels; recommend decision duplicate into Ginkgo and add those OpenFOAM numbers as an integration note on the Ginkgo entry. Metadata: 41 stars, 14 forks, last commit 2026-05-09, active.
